title: Sensor
description:
## Context
Trigger side of the CI pipeline - routes GitHub push/tag webhooks to the WorkflowTemplate's two entrypoints.

## Design
k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/clustertop-sensor.yml, modeled on domain-check-sensor.yml's two triggers (push-to-main -> build, tag v* -> release) but WITHOUT its ci-author-filter (clustertop's build path never commits back to the repo, so there's no self-trigger loop to guard against).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] git pull --rebase origin main run before editing
- [ ] kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f clustertop-sensor.yml validates against the Sensor CRD schema
- [ ] git push origin main succeeds

## Notes


Owns: declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/clustertop-sensor.yml
close_reason: kubectl apply --dry-run=client validated cleanly against the real Sensor CRD on iad-ci. git push origin main succeeded on the first try.

title: WorkflowTemplate
description:
## Context
New Argo CI pipeline, modeled on domain-check but trimmed (no docker-build/VERSION-bump, since this ships a binary not a container image). See docs/research/ci-pipeline-pattern.md and docs/research/iad-ci-resource-budget.md.

## Design
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/clustertop-workflowtemplate.yml in declarative-config. Two entrypoints: build (push to main -> quality-gate: go vet ./..., go test -race ./...) and release (tag v* -> quality-gate + goreleaser-release). quality-gate: golang:1.26, request 500m/1Gi, limit 1000m/2Gi. goreleaser-release: golang:1.26-alpine, request 1000m/2Gi, limit 2000m/4Gi. Auth via existing github-webhook-secret (GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN), no new secret.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] declarative-config git pull --rebase origin main run before editing, per that repo's CLAUDE.md
- [ ] kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f clustertop-workflowtemplate.yml validates against the Workflow CRD schema
- [ ] resource requests/limits satisfy: limit <= 2x request, memory limit <= 6Gi, cpu limit <= 3.50 (all checked by inspection against docs/research/iad-ci-resource-budget.md's table)
- [ ] git push origin main succeeds on the first try or after one rebase-retry per that repo's git discipline

## Notes


Owns: declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/clustertop-workflowtemplate.yml
close_reason: kubectl apply --dry-run=client validated cleanly against the real Workflow CRD on iad-ci. Resource requests/limits satisfy the <=2x-request/<=6Gi/<=3.50c rules from docs/research/iad-ci-resource-budget.md. git push origin main succeeded on the first try (no rebase needed).

title: Genesis: clustertop Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
Go + Bubble Tea TUI polling every fleet cluster's read-only kubectl-proxy for
live node status, ships via a new Argo CI pipeline (Go + GoReleaser -> GitHub
Release). Reviewed twice (structural + adversarial gap hunt); zero
undeliverable tasks as of the second pass.

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0: Repo hosting bootstrap
- [ ] Phase 1: Core fetch, no UI
- [ ] Phase 2: Bubble Tea static render
- [ ] Phase 3: Concurrency, refresh, responsive layout
- [ ] Phase 4: CI pipeline
- [ ] Phase 5: sync-clusters subcommand
close_reason: All 6 phases complete: repo hosting bootstrap, core fetch, Bubble Tea UI, responsive layout, sync-clusters regenerator, and CI pipeline. Real end-to-end verification: go vet/test pass in a genuine clean-clone CI pod (caught and fixed a real go.mod/go.sum omission bug that only a real CI run, not local dev, could catch). WorkflowTemplate/Sensor/EventSource are live on the iad-ci cluster and dry-run-validated. The final full pipeline run (build reaching Succeeded, a real v0.1.0 GitHub release) is blocked by a genuine PRE-EXISTING iad-ci capacity crisis unrelated to clustertop -- 38 already-unscheduled pods wanting 29c/56Gi against a 15c/26Gi cluster, plus an unexplained node-class selector -- out of scope to fix here; flagged to the user separately.

title: Phase 1: Core fetch, no UI
description: See docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.
close_reason: All 5 Phase 1 tasks closed and verified: go.mod/main.go skeleton, config loader, clusters.yaml, k8s HTTP client, fetch/timeout wrapper + NodeRow. go build ./... and go vet ./... both clean.

title: Model/Msg/Cmd skeleton
description:
## Context
Core Bubble Tea state machine. Concurrency/fault-isolation design fully specified in docs/research/bubbletea-fault-isolation.md.

## Design
package ui. ClusterState{Cluster config.Cluster; Status ClusterStatus; Nodes []fetch.NodeRow; Err error; LastFetch time.Time; Fetching bool; Table table.Model}. ClusterStatus tri-state (Pending/OK/Error) per plan.md section 4. Model{Clusters []ClusterState; idx map[string]int; Width, Height int; RefreshEvery, FetchTimeout time.Duration}. tickMsg, fetchResultMsg{ClusterName string; Nodes []fetch.NodeRow; Err error}. fetchClusterCmd(c config.Cluster, timeout time.Duration) tea.Cmd, fetchAllCmd(clusters []config.Cluster, timeout time.Duration) tea.Cmd (tea.Batch of per-cluster cmds), tickCmd(every time.Duration) tea.Cmd.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go build ./internal/ui/... succeeds (may still be a partial package pending later Phase 2 tasks in the same phase, but these specific types/functions compile standalone with fetch/config already available from Phase 1)
- [ ] Model.Init() returns tea.Batch(fetchAllCmd(...), tickCmd(...))

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/model.go, internal/ui/msg.go, internal/ui/cmd.go
close_reason: go build ./... succeeds; Init() returns tea.Batch(fetchAllCmd(...), tickCmd(...)) per code; end-to-end confirmed working via live tmux smoke test against the real 8-cluster fleet.

title: Fault-isolation integration test
description:
## Context
The single highest-value test in this project per docs/research/bubbletea-fault-isolation.md - proves one dead cluster can't block or blank the rest, without needing a real cluster.

## Design
Spin up several httptest.Server instances (one deliberately sleeping past FetchTimeout), wire them into real config.Cluster entries, run the real fetchAllCmd against them, and inspect the resulting fetchResultMsg batch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/ui/... (integration_test.go portion) passes
- [ ] test asserts: the 7 healthy servers' results all arrive with Err==nil within a bounded time window (well under FetchTimeout*2), and the 1 slow server's result arrives with a non-nil Err at approximately FetchTimeout, not blocking the others' delivery

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/integration_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/ui/... TestFaultIsolation_OneSlowClusterDoesNotBlockOthers passes: all 7 healthy clusters return correct results, the slow cluster times out with a non-nil error, and the whole batch completes within timeout bounds rather than waiting out the slow handler's full 2s sleep.

title: Phase 4: CI pipeline
description: Depends on Phase 0 + Phase 3. Spans clustertop + declarative-config repos. See docs/plan/plan.md Phase 4.
close_reason: All 4 Phase 4 tasks closed and verified via kubectl dry-run against real CRDs: WorkflowTemplate, Sensor, EventSource entry, .goreleaser.yml. Also caught and fixed a real operational gotcha: bumped webhook-registration-retry since the running EventSource pod was already 16h old and wouldn't have picked up the new clustertop webhook without a forced restart.

title: Phase 5: sync-clusters subcommand
description: Depends on Phase 1 only; independent of Phases 2-4. See docs/plan/plan.md Phase 5.
close_reason: Phase 5 complete: manifest scanner + regenerator closed and verified against the real declarative-config checkout with zero drift.

title: .goreleaser.yml
description:
## Context
Config the goreleaser-release WorkflowTemplate step reads to actually build and publish the release.

## Design
version: 2. CGO_ENABLED=0 builds for linux/darwin x amd64/arm64. tar.gz archives, checksums.txt. release.github pointing at jedarden/clustertop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] goreleaser check (run locally, requires goreleaser installed, or defer to the first real Phase 4 tag-push run per plan.md section 7's release verification) reports the config valid
- [ ] go build ./... still succeeds independent of this file (goreleaser config doesn't affect the Go build itself)

## Notes


Owns: .goreleaser.yml
close_reason: goreleaser check (v2.17.1, current latest release) validates the config with zero errors. go build ./... unaffected, confirming the goreleaser config doesn't interact with the regular Go build.

title: Phase 2: Bubble Tea static render
description: Depends on Phase 1. See docs/plan/plan.md Phase 2.
close_reason: All 5 Phase 2 tasks closed and verified: Model/Msg/Cmd skeleton, table rendering, view+styles, keybindings, ui.Run(). Live-tested against the real 8-cluster fleet via tmux capture, including catching and fixing a real label-key bug (POOL/TYPE).

title: ui.Run() real implementation
description:
## Context
Replaces Phase 1's main.go stub call target with the real Bubble Tea program entrypoint.

## Design
func Run() error constructing the initial Model from a loaded clusters.yaml (default path "clusters.yaml" relative to cwd) and running tea.NewProgram(model).Run().

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go build ./... succeeds with main.go's ui.Run() stub replaced by this real implementation
- [ ] go run . against a real or fixture clusters.yaml starts without an immediate panic/crash (interactive - verified manually or via the tmux capture step in plan.md section 7, not a unit test)

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/run.go
close_reason: go build ./... succeeds with the real implementation in place of the Phase 1 stub. go run . against the real clusters.yaml ran repeatedly via tmux smoke tests without any panic or crash, rendering live fleet data correctly.

title: Tick/refresh + WindowSizeMsg breakpoint
description:
## Context
Auto-refresh loop and responsive layout are the two behaviors plan.md's mockups (section 1) depend on.

## Design
On tickMsg: mark all ClusterState.Fetching=true, return tea.Batch(fetchAllCmd(...), tickCmd(RefreshEvery)) to re-arm. On tea.WindowSizeMsg: store Width/Height in Model, recompute per-cluster table column set (drop POOL/TYPE and VERSION columns below ~100 cols per plan.md section 1's breakpoint), wrap output in bubbles/viewport sized to Height.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go build ./... succeeds
- [ ] covered by model_test.go (next task) and the live tmux-capture verification in plan.md section 7

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/model.go, internal/ui/view.go (edits to files Phase 2 created)
close_reason: go build/vet clean. Live-tested via tmux resize against the real fleet at 200 and 60 cols and back — correct column switch, no stale-row artifacts, no crash. Caught and fixed a real bubbles/table panic on narrowing that only showed up under live resize, not in the earlier static smoke test.

title: Per-cluster fetch/timeout wrapper + NodeRow
description:
## Context
internal/ui needs cluster node data as ready-to-render rows, with per-cluster timeout isolation already applied. Per the phase-order fix in plan.md section 2/4: this package owns NodeRow and the corev1.Node mapping, NOT internal/ui.

## Design
package fetch. NodeRow{Name, Roles, PoolType, Version, Age string; Ready bool; Warning string}. FromNode(n corev1.Node) NodeRow reading node-role.kubernetes.io/* labels for Roles, servers.ngpc.rxt.io/type for PoolType (docs/research/node-metadata-keys.md), Warning set to "on-demand pool" if PoolType=="ondemand" or "scale-down tainted" if any taint key contains DeletionCandidateOfClusterAutoscaler. FetchClusterNodes(ctx, c config.Cluster, timeout time.Duration) ([]NodeRow, error) wraps k8sclient.FetchNodes in context.WithTimeout, maps every node via FromNode, always returns (rows, err), never panics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/fetch/... passes
- [ ] table-driven test over corev1.Node fixtures: Ready condition true/false/missing/Unknown all map correctly to NodeRow.Ready
- [ ] fixture with node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane label -> Roles contains control-plane; no role labels -> Roles == "<none>"
- [ ] fixture with servers.ngpc.rxt.io/type=ondemand -> Warning == "on-demand pool"
- [ ] fixture with a taint Key containing DeletionCandidateOfClusterAutoscaler -> Warning == "scale-down tainted"
- [ ] FetchClusterNodes against a slow httptest.Server past its timeout returns promptly at the timeout boundary with a non-nil error, not blocking past it

## Notes


Owns: internal/fetch/fetch.go, internal/fetch/fetch_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/fetch/... passes all cases: Ready true/false/Unknown/missing/no-conditions, role-label extraction incl. <none> fallback, on-demand-pool warning, autoscaler-taint warning, no-warning default, and FetchClusterNodes bounding a 2s-slow handler to its 100ms timeout.

title: go.mod + main.go skeleton
description:
## Context
Every other Go file in this repo needs a module to belong to and an entrypoint that dispatches to it. plan.md DECIDED the module path.

## Design
module github.com/jedarden/clustertop. main.go: if os.Args[1]=="sync-clusters", call syncclusters.Run(os.Args[2:]); else call ui.Run(). Both Run() funcs stubbed to `return errors.New("not implemented")` so this compiles now and is never edited again by later phases.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go build ./... succeeds with only the stub packages present
- [ ] go run . sync-clusters prints the not-implemented error and exits non-zero
- [ ] go run . (no args) prints the not-implemented error and exits non-zero

## Notes


Owns: go.mod, go.sum, main.go
close_reason: go build ./... succeeds; go run . and go run . sync-clusters both exit 1 with the expected not-implemented stub error. Verified by command, not inspection.

title: View composition + styles
description:
## Context
Section chrome around each cluster's table - header, UNREACHABLE banner, staleness indicator - none of which fits a bubbles component, per docs/plan/plan.md architecture notes.

## Design
lipgloss styles for Ready (green)/NotReady (red)/Unreachable (banner style)/Warning (yellow ⚠). Per-cluster header line: "<name> — <ready>/<total> Ready" or "<name> — UNREACHABLE" with the error text and last-seen duration when Status==StatusError.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go build ./internal/ui/... succeeds
- [ ] manual smoke check deferred to Phase 3's tmux-capture verification step in plan.md section 7 (rendering fidelity isn't practically unit-tested per docs/plan/plan.md Testing notes)

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/view.go, internal/ui/style.go
close_reason: go build ./... succeeds. Manual smoke check (this bead's stated deferred-to-Phase-3 criterion) already done and exceeded: live tmux capture against the real 8-cluster fleet confirmed correct rendering, including catching and fixing a real POOL/TYPE label bug.

title: EventSource entry
description:
## Context
Registers the webhook endpoint for clustertop so GitHub push events actually reach the Sensor above.

## Design
Add a clustertop: block to k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/github-eventsource.yml, next to the existing domain-check: entry - endpoint: /clustertop, port: "12000", same apiToken/webhookSecret pattern every existing entry uses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] git pull --rebase origin main run before editing
- [ ] kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f github-eventsource.yml validates against the EventSource CRD schema
- [ ] the new block is byte-for-byte structurally identical to the existing domain-check: block except for the repo name/endpoint
- [ ] git push origin main succeeds

## Notes


Owns: declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/github-eventsource.yml (edits existing shared file, does not own it)
close_reason: kubectl apply --dry-run=client validated cleanly against the real EventSource CRD. Confirmed byte-identical to the domain-check: block modulo the repo name (first diff check had a regex boundary bug that accidentally included my own leading comment; corrected boundary shows zero diff). git push origin main succeeded on the first try.

title: Cluster config loader
description:
## Context
internal/fetch and internal/ui both need a typed Cluster/Config to work with, loaded from clusters.yaml.

## Design
package config. Config{Clusters []Cluster}. Cluster{Name, Endpoint, Route string; Notes string `yaml:"notes,omitempty"`}. LoadClusters(path string) (Config, error) using gopkg.in/yaml.v3 default (non-strict) decode. Error only when Clusters is empty; unknown YAML keys ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/config/... passes
- [ ] table-driven test covers: valid yaml, missing endpoint field (should still load - no field is required except the list being non-empty), unknown extra key ignored without error, empty clusters list returns an error

## Notes


Owns: internal/config/config.go, internal/config/config_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/config/... passes all 5 cases: valid load, unknown-key-ignored, missing-field-still-loads, empty-list errors, file-not-found errors.

title: Table rendering
description:
## Context
Renders fetch.NodeRow data into a bubbles/table per cluster section. NOT the corev1.Node mapping (Phase 1 owns that) - this is a later transformation, business rows to widget rows.

## Design
toTableRows(nodes []fetch.NodeRow) []table.Row. One bubbles/table.Model constructed per cluster (columns: NODE, STATUS, ROLES, POOL/TYPE, VERSION, AGE), never .Focus()ed since keybindings are minimal (q/r only, no per-row selection).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/ui/... (table_test.go portion) passes
- [ ] deterministic string-output test: a fixture []fetch.NodeRow produces the exact expected []table.Row cell values
- [ ] a NodeRow with non-empty Warning produces a row with the warning marker present in output

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/table.go, internal/ui/table_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/ui/... passes: deterministic cell-value test, warning-marker-present test, empty-input test.

title: K8s HTTP client
description:
## Context
The only network call this tool ever makes: GET /api/v1/nodes against an unauthenticated in-cluster kubectl-proxy. See docs/research/k8s-client-choice.md for why this is plain net/http, not client-go.

## Design
package k8sclient. FetchNodes(ctx context.Context, endpoint string) (*corev1.NodeList, error) using k8s.io/api/core/v1 for the response type only (no client-go). http.NewRequestWithContext + http.DefaultClient.Do; non-200 and decode-failure both become errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/k8sclient/... passes
- [ ] httptest.Server fixture returning valid NodeList JSON -> FetchNodes returns it with nil error
- [ ] httptest.Server fixture returning malformed JSON -> FetchNodes returns a non-nil error, no panic
- [ ] httptest.Server fixture returning HTTP 500 -> FetchNodes returns a non-nil error mentioning the status code
- [ ] connection-refused (server closed before request) -> FetchNodes returns a non-nil error, no panic
- [ ] httptest.Server handler that sleeps past a short context.WithTimeout -> FetchNodes returns context.DeadlineExceeded-wrapping error within the timeout window, not after

## Notes


Owns: internal/k8sclient/client.go, internal/k8sclient/client_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/k8sclient/... passes all 5 fixture cases: 200-valid, malformed-JSON, HTTP 500, connection-refused, and context-timeout bounding the call (verified client aborts well before the handler's artificial 2s delay).

title: clusters.yaml
description:
## Context
Static, checked-in endpoint config for all 8 fleet clusters, sourced from docs/research/cluster-endpoints.md.

## Design
Exact 8-entry content is given verbatim in docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1 (copy it exactly - FQDN endpoints, not short hostnames, per the DECIDED row in plan.md section 4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] all 8 cluster names from docs/research/cluster-endpoints.md's table are present with matching endpoint and route values

## Notes


Owns: clusters.yaml
close_reason: Parses cleanly via PyYAML; all 8 cluster names match docs/research/cluster-endpoints.md's table exactly, endpoint/route values transcribed verbatim.

title: Keybindings
description:
## Context
Deliberately minimal interaction surface.

## Design
key.Binding for quit (q, ctrl+c) and refresh (r). bubbles/help wiring for a footer hint line.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go build ./internal/ui/... succeeds
- [ ] Update() on a KeyMsg matching quit returns a Cmd that is tea.Quit
- [ ] Update() on a KeyMsg matching refresh returns fetchAllCmd(...) and marks all ClusterState.Fetching=true

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/keys.go

title: Create + wire remotes
description:
## Context
New repo needs to exist on Forgejo (source of truth) with a GitHub push mirror before Phase 4's webhook-triggered CI can fire. See /home/coding/CLAUDE.md 'Git Hosting'.

## Design
Follow the exact 5-step flow in /home/coding/CLAUDE.md: create Forgejo repo via API, create GitHub repo via gh, set up Forgejo->GitHub push mirror (sync_on_commit: true), set local origin=Forgejo only, push initial scaffold commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] curl to Forgejo API returns 201 and the repo exists at git.ardenone.com/jedarden/clustertop
- [ ] gh repo view jedarden/clustertop succeeds
- [ ] git remote -v shows origin pointing at git.ardenone.com only, no github.com remote configured client-side
- [ ] git push -u origin main succeeds; git log on Forgejo web UI shows the scaffold commit

## Notes
Never set up client-side dual-push per org convention.

Owns: none (operational, no source files)
close_reason: Forgejo repo created (201), GitHub mirror created + push-mirror configured (sync_on_commit), origin=Forgejo only confirmed via git remote -v, scaffold commit ed6d644 pushed and verified present on both Forgejo and GitHub mirror.

title: Phase 3: Concurrency, refresh, responsive layout
description: Depends on Phase 2. See docs/plan/plan.md Phase 3.
close_reason: All 3 Phase 3 tasks closed and verified: responsive tick/refresh/WindowSizeMsg breakpoint (with a real crash caught and fixed via live testing), model transition tests, fault-isolation integration test.

title: Manifest scanner + regenerator
description:
## Context
Anti-drift mechanism for clusters.yaml - the exact problem that surfaced live this session (ardenone-hub stale in docs for weeks post-decommission). See docs/research/sync-clusters-source-manifests.md for the two-manifest-path logic this must implement.

## Design
package syncclusters. For each cluster dir in a given declarative-config checkout path: (1) if <cluster>/devpod-observer/kubectl-proxy.yml's Service has a tailscale.com/hostname annotation directly, use it, route=direct-tailscale-operator; (2) else read <cluster>/traefik/tailscale-service.yml's tailscale.com/hostname annotation, confirm a kubectl-tcp port is exposed, route=traefik-kubectl-tcp; (3) neither shape found -> skip with a logged warning, not a fatal error. Regenerate clusters.yaml from the results.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/syncclusters/... passes
- [ ] fixture directory shaped like a direct-tailscale-operator cluster (kubectl-proxy.yml with the annotation) is correctly parsed
- [ ] fixture directory shaped like a Traefik-routed cluster (kubectl-proxy.yml without the annotation + a traefik/tailscale-service.yml with it) is correctly parsed
- [ ] fixture directory matching neither shape is skipped with a warning, not a crash or fatal error
- [ ] go run . sync-clusters --declarative-config-path ~/declarative-config against the real repo, then git diff --exit-code clusters.yaml is empty (plan.md section 7's Phase 5 verification)

## Notes


Owns: internal/syncclusters/sync.go, internal/syncclusters/sync_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/syncclusters/... passes all 4 fixture cases (direct-operator shape, traefik-routed shape, unrecognized-shape skip, non-cluster-dir ignored). Ran for real against ~/declarative-config: output diffs empty against the hand-written clusters.yaml — exact match, zero drift.

title: Model transition tests
description:
## Context
Pure state-machine correctness, especially the stale-on-error guarantee that is this whole project's core requirement.

## Design
Table-driven (Model, Msg) -> (Model, Cmd) tests, no I/O, no tea.Program.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] go test ./internal/ui/... (model_test.go portion) passes
- [ ] test: feed a successful fetchResultMsg, then an error fetchResultMsg for the same cluster; assert Status flips to StatusError while Nodes from the first message are still present, not cleared
- [ ] test: KeyMsg for quit returns a Cmd equal to tea.Quit

## Notes


Owns: internal/ui/model_test.go
close_reason: go test ./internal/ui/... passes all 7 new cases, including the WindowSizeMsg column-count toggle test that reproduces the panic fixed in ct-4ep.
